rules.question: Which generation is this library file?
rules.decision: D115 task A1-6a (user, 2026-10-14: what is an old version is derived once)
must_match: if (!has_column("charts", "sig")) exec("ALTER TABLE charts ADD COLUMN sig TEXT");
Stmt s = prepare_read(db_, "SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table'");
rules.note: Every older layout is told apart by its tables, read in one place, so a probe of a file's tables or schema slot anywhere else in shipped code is a second answer. Hydra never writes the user_version slot (D53 item 1). path_report_window's has_column is a report column, not a table's. Decided by: D115 task A1-6a, replacing the J4-2 schema row (D53, D54)

must_match: if (std::optional<std::string> why = rename_file(path, old_path(path))) return why;
rules.note: The app's open is the only thing that moves a library file, and it moves it to set_aside_path's name; the command-line tools refuse an old file and never rename it. Decided by: D115 task A1-6a

rules.question: What does an open do with a library file too old to convert?
rules.owner: OldFilePolicy in src/store/library_file.h, named by each shipped caller

rules.question: How many library rows does a chart on a page count as when the library doesn't list it?
must_not_match: for (const auto& [md5, n] : store.library_copies()) by_hash[normalize_chart_hash(md5)] += n;
rules.note: A chart on a page that the library doesn't list still counts. One function says how much; a page that looks a chart up in the copies map itself, or starts its count at a default, is a second answer. Decided by: D77 item 2, D79 item 3 (task COUNT-P)

rules.question: How many charts does a page or its tool count?
rules.owner: each row's copies from RecordStore::copies_of, added up by generate_report, tally_fill_rows and the fill page's stats() through the payload's "k"
must_match: const n = s => rows.filter(r => r.status === s).length;
must_not_match: const n = s => charts(rows.filter(r => r.status === s));
rules.note: The path report and the fill comparison count charts by adding up each row's copies, in C++ and in the fill page's script alike. Counting rows instead drops every extra copy. The leaderboard comparison counts posted scores, not charts (D79), so it is not scanned. Decided by: D79 item 3 (task COUNT-P)

rules.question: When does the WAL checkpoint threshold change, and when is the log emptied?
rules.note: D86 item 3: the checkpoint threshold changes only while a batch runs, and the log is emptied only when it ends. A second place that sets either one is a second answer. Decided by: D86 item 3 (task W1)

rules.question: Is a transaction still open, or has sqlite already rolled it back?

owner_lines.why: transaction_open, the owner: rollback_if_open and save_analysis call it

rules.note: After a failure, rollback_if_open and a grouped save_analysis both need to know whether sqlite already rolled the transaction back. Only the helper asks sqlite; record_store.cpp is not exempt as a file, so a second ask there fails like one anywhere else.

rules.question: Could this stored fingerprint ever show a chart unchanged?

owner_lines.line_text: inline bool sig_can_show_unchanged(const std::string& sig) { return !sig.empty(); }
owner_lines.why: sig_can_show_unchanged, the owner: chart_library_cache, sig_unchanged and ViewJob::run call it

rules.note: An empty fingerprint is what a gone file or a folder chart without its song.ini gives, so it can never show a chart unchanged. The cache read, the rescan's test and the click's save all ask store::sig_can_show_unchanged, which sits in store/ so every layer can call it. Only a variable named for a fingerprint is caught, as the three callers name theirs. Decided by: D96 (an empty fingerprint never shows a chart unchanged) and its follow-up in the audit fix decisions

rules.question: Which files make up a database on disk?
must_not_match: "' is open in another program: its -wal or -shm file stayed ");
rules.note: A WAL database's log and index sit beside it under SQLite's two suffixes. The upgrade's file rule names them once; code that sweeps or checks a database's files asks it (with_side_files, remove_with_side_files, side_files_present). Decided by: derive-once review of the DBUP join (F4); ADR 0026, the upgrade
